text:
maya: Heads-up — ran into a routing ambiguity in the gateway while testing canary headers. TL;DR: header-based canary route is being shadowed by a path wildcard fallback.

jon: repro steps?

maya: create two routes:
```
- route A: match { host: '*.prod.internal', path: '/svc/orders/**', header: 'x-canary=true' } -> service orders@canary
- route B: match { host: '*.prod.internal', path: '/svc/orders/**' } -> service orders@stable weight=100
```
send request with `x-canary=true` and it hits orders@stable.

ashley: oof. expected header match to win. Is the matcher engine ordering by path length only?

tomas: current algo: score = literal_segment_count + (host_specificity * 10). We don't include header match in scoring right now. So header routes can lose to numerically higher path scores.

jon: that seems wrong for canaries. Headers are explicit intent, should have higher priority than wildcards unless an exact host+path exact route exists.

maya: agreed. I hacked a local comparator:
```pseudo
score = (exact_host? 1000 : 0) + (num_literal_path_segments * 10) + (has_header ? 500 : 0) - (num_wildcards * 20)
```
This made the header route win in our tests.

ashley: Where does route creation order fit in? We've seen older routes outrank newer ones previously.

tomas: creation_time is the final tie-breaker currently. But relying on it is brittle. We should expose an explicit `priority` field for operators + add deterministic comparator.

jon: Proposal: change default comparator to include header matches and query-params as "specificity tokens". Then: 1) exact host > host-wildcard, 2) header/query presence increases specificity, 3) path literal segments count, 4) fewer wildcards, 5) explicit priority, 6) creation_time.

maya: +1. Also: need to handle multi-header routes (e.g., two headers required) — specificity should grow with header count, not just boolean.

ashley: UX note — when users write overlapping routes we should show a warning in Console: "Route X will shadow Route Y under condition Z (headers/path)" with a preview example request.

infra-bot: deploy job started for gateway matcher change (ci-1234) :construction:

jon: one more edge-case — header-only routes that don't include path/host constraints. If header-only routes get high specificity they could steal a lot of traffic. Maybe require at least one host/path literal unless user sets `priority` > 0?

tomas: good call. We can require header-only routes to set `priority` or opt-in `allow-header-only: true`. Default denies implicit hijack.

maya: I'll draft an RFC for comparator changes + Console UX warning. Will include sample comparator pseudocode and a migration plan (backfill explicit priorities for legacy routes).

jon: thanks — please add test cases for: header vs wildcard, multi-header specificity, header-only protections, and creation_time tie-breakers.

ashley: and perf — comparator runs on every config reload; make sure it's O(n log n) sort-friendly, not quadratic when evaluating specificity.

maya: noted. filing RFC now -> https://redwood.internal/rfcs/rfc-gateway-specificity (draft)

infra-bot: deploy job succeeded (ci-1234) :white_check_mark: 

tomas: follow-up: after RFC I'll open a small PR to add `priority` field and the warning UI.

maya: thanks team, gonna block on this until PR lands, holding canary rollouts for orders by default.
